ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.59
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.59 in backend/package.json and npm-app/package.json. Unused `createPatch` import removed from backend/src/main-prompt.ts. No user-facing changes.

eli5.text: The software's internal version number was bumped to 1.0.59 and some leftover code importing an unused feature was cleaned up. No new features were added or bugs fixed for users, it is behind-the-scenes maintenance that developers would notice in the project files, but end users won't see any difference in how the app works.

ai.title: Copy tree-sitter queries in common build
ai.summary: Updated `common` package build script to copy `src/codemap/tree-sitter-queries` into `dist/codemap/` after TypeScript compilation. This ensures tree-sitter queries are available in the distributed build output. Version bumped to 1.0.60 for `backend` and `npm-app`.

eli5.text: The assistant's build process now automatically copies a set of rule files (used to understand code structure) into the final packaged output, so they are included whenever the software is built and deployed. Anyone running the latest assistant build will have these rule files available at runtime without needing them provided separately. If you checked the built folder, you'd see the rule files present alongside the compiled code, and the package version on the distribution servers has been updated to reflect this.

ai.title: Add troubleshooting section to README
ai.summary: Added a Troubleshooting section to npm-app/README.md addressing global installation permission errors. Recommends using version managers like nvm for OSX/Unix and nvm-windows for Windows, including installation commands and links.

eli5.text: The guide that explains how to use the tool now includes a new section that helps if you get an error message saying you don't have permission to install or run it. It tells you to install a helper program first, and gives different instructions depending on whether you use a Mac/Linux or Windows computer, including links to download pages. This is helpful for anyone trying to set up the tool who encounters this specific permission error, and is available now.

ai.title: Add README, .env.example, dev scripts
ai.summary: Added root README.md documenting Manicode features, usage, and local setup. Created backend/.env.example with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPEN_AI_KEY, HELICONE_API_KEY placeholders. Updated package.json with dev:start-client and dev:start-server scripts, added ts-node dependency, and specified bun@1.1.27 packageManager.

eli5.text: If you open the project folder now, you'll find a friendly guide at the top level that explains what the assistant does and how to run it, plus a ready-made file you copy and fill in with your artificial intelligence account keys. When you type the new run commands from a terminal, the app launches its front-end and the behind-the-scenes helper at the same time without needing to remember long addresses or file locations. The project is pinned to a single version of its tool manager today, so the setup described in the guide will behave the same on every person's computer, and the added helper package simply lets those run commands stay written in plain English.

ai.title: Add start-dev.sh for local development setup
ai.summary: New `start-dev.sh` script automates starting server and client in separate macOS Terminal windows. It waits for server readiness on port 4242 before launching client. `package.json` scripts renamed `dev:start-server`/`dev:start-client` to `start-server`/`start-client`. README updated with usage instructions and macOS limitation note.

eli5.text: When you run the new starter command on a Mac, the app now opens two separate windows for you: one for the app's engine and one for the visual app. The visual part only launches after the engine confirms it is fully ready, so you won't see connection errors. The setup steps were also rewritten in the guide to match this easier one-command flow, with a note that it only works on macOS for now.

ai.title: Update npm-app README troubleshooting section
ai.summary: Refined Troubleshooting section in `npm-app/README.md`. Converted inline advice into hyperlinks for node version managers and adjusted heading levels from H3 to H4. Minor copy edits improved readability.

eli5.text: The built-in guide for getting help when things go wrong has been tidied up and made easier to follow. If you run into installation problems, the troubleshooting steps now link directly to the recommended tools and use clearer section headings. The advice itself hasn't changed, just how it's presented.

ai.title: Add Manicode README and local dev startup scripts
ai.summary: Added comprehensive README.md for Manicode, detailing features, usage, and local setup instructions. Created backend/.env.example with placeholder keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, and Helicone. Updated package.json scripts to separate client and server startup commands (start-client, start-server) and added ts-node dependency. Introduced start-dev.sh to orchestrate local development by launching server and client in separate terminal windows.

eli5.text: A new guide was added that explains how to start the coding assistant's two-part system on your own computer. It creates a helper file with placeholder slots for three AI provider keys, and the main start command now launches the background engine and the interactive chat window separately instead of only the chat. A single script opens both pieces in their own terminal windows so you can see both the tool's log output and your conversation side by side.
